sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER  WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:36852  CRL.P No. 8307 of 2024  ORAL ORDER Accused No.1 in Crime No.36/2024 registered by Mahalakshmipuram Police Station, Bengaluru City for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 498A, 511, 302, 120B & 201 R/w 34 of IPC is before this Court seeking regular bail.
2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.36/2024 was registered by Mahalakshmipuram Police Station, Bengaluru City initially for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC against the petitioner herein, on the basis of first information dated 05.02.2024 received from Smt. Sarojamma W/o Late Hulluraiah,
who is the mother of deceased Pushpalatha @ Prema.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner was arrested and remanded to judicial custody on 07.02.2024.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed against two NC: 2024:KHC:36852 persons for the aforesaid offences.
The petitioner herein is arraigned as accused No.1 in the charge sheet.
4. The bail application filed by the petitioner before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.5266/2024 was dismissed on 02.07.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he is required to take care of his two minor children aged about 11 and 9 years respectively, who are now staying with his aged father.
He submits that entire case of the prosecution is based on circumstantial evidence.
The allegation against the petitioner is that he had conspired with accused No.2 to commit the murder of deceased.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
He submits that the petitioner had motive to commit murder of his wife and he had conspired with NC: 2024:KHC:36852 accused No.2.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: The material on record would go to show that marriage of the petitioner with deceased Pushpalatha was solemnized in the year 2010 and from the wedlock they have two children.

On 05.02.2024, the dead body of Pushpalatha was found in her house and since the first informant suspected the hand of the petitioner in the death of her daughter, she had submitted a first information, based on which, FIR in Crime No.36/2024 was initially registered against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC.

During the course of investigation,
the petitioner was arrested on 07.02.2024.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed against two persons.
The petitioner is arraigned as accused No.1 in the charge sheet.

8. As per the charge sheet allegation, the petitioner suspected the chastity of his wife and he was NC:
2024:KHC:36852 regularly torturing her in his house.
It is in this background, he had allegedly hatched conspiracy with accused No.2, who was earlier his colleague and had promised to pay a sum of Rs.3 lakhs for committing murder of his wife.
In furtherance of such conspiracy, accused No.2 allegedly had gone to the house of the petitioner and had knocked the door of house.
When deceased opened the door, he represented himself as courier boy and entered the house.
Thereafter, he allegedly caught hold of Pushpalatha and closed her mouth and nose with his hands.
As a result, she fell down unconscious.
Thereafter, accused No.2 allegedly intended to have sex with Pushpalatha.
In the meanwhile, she regained conscious.
Accused No.2 thereafter strangulated the neck of Pushpalatha with his hands and committed her murder and hanged her dead body to iron rod of the window and had left the place.
The entire case of the prosecution is based on circumstantial evidence.
The allegation against petitioner is that he had conspired with accused No.2 and allegedly paid certain amount to commit the murder of deceased Pushpalatha.
There is absolutely no material on record to show that the petitioner had paid any amount to accused No.2 to commit the murder of his wife Pushpalatha.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he is in custody from 07.02.2024.

The material on record would go to show that he is required to take care of his two minor children,
who are now staying with his aged father.
10. Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that, the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

11. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
